summary: CEIR-21 sec-51 ceir.tensor: PRESERVE TENSOR SEMANTICS above raw dispatch — the high-level tensor value IR over the CEIR-3d Tensor TYPE (members = [element, shape]; declared since 3d). ⛔ sec-70: DO NOT prematurely lower a tensor op to a standalone kernel / flatten a tensor graph to 100 CKIR dispatches before the compiler decides whether the device runs it as ONE native graph program (D3D12 MLIR Programs / VK_ARM_data_graph / vendor NPU / CUDA Graphs) — so EVERY op is Pure + typed NoSemantics + carries NO kernel_ref, NO lowering hook. This slice (21b) declares the STRUCTURAL SIX (the 20a consumer-need subset — the ops that cover every distinct shape-semantics class, NOT all of sec-51's 13): elementwise · broadcast · reshape · transpose · reduce · matmul. ⛔ NO-FOLLOW / NAME-FORWARD (declared != implemented; a later band with a real consumer, never a silent subset): FFT is ADDED here in CEIR-22a (tensor.fft, c2c SPLIT re/im — the sec-59 fft leg); solve / decomposition-hooks -> ceir.linalg (CEIR-22, the sec-52 identities); gather/scatter / scans / sort-topk / convolution -> named-forward rows; sparse/ragged forms + quantized element types -> CEIR-23 (ceir.sparse / ceir.quant). The element type is a CEIR-3a scalar kind (f16/bf16/f32/f64/int/uint); fp8 + block-quantized dtypes are CEIR-23. ⛔ NO `tensor.constant` (a literal payload = blob serialization, a whole design; a tensor VALUE seeds from block args / a resource.import — data I/O rides the v14-I/O reuse at the consumer band). ⛔ THE TARGET SHAPE RIDES THE RESULT TYPE (not a Shape operand): a shape-changing op result is `!tensor<element, target_shape>`, and find_tensor_misuse VALIDATES that target against the inputs (the 21a shape.make result-identity precedent). ⛔ I6 — find_tensor_misuse switches on op NAME + TypeKind, never op.kind. crd-ceir NEVER links gpu-context (I3/I4); ZERO renderer changes.

ops.name: broadcast
ops.summary: Broadcast one tensor UP to the result's shape (input.shape broadcasts to the target result shape).
ops.docs: tensor.broadcast(%input) -> %result. Broadcast a tensor up to the result's (larger) shape (sec-51 broadcast); the target rides the result type. Pure. find_tensor_misuse: operand + result Tensor-kinded; input.element == result.element (TensorElementMismatch); the input broadcasts TO the target ⇒ shapes_broadcast_result(input.shape, result.shape) == result.shape (BroadcastResultMismatch), Unknown -> ACCEPT. STRUCTURAL (1 operand, 1 result, no attrs): the generated verify_broadcast.

operands.name: input
operands.doc: the tensor broadcast up (a 3d Tensor); each of its axes is 1 or == the target's.

results.name: result
results.doc: element == input's; shape == the TARGET (a supershape input broadcasts to). find_tensor_misuse checks input broadcasts to it.

ops.name: elementwise
ops.summary: A binary elementwise op (fn closed vocab) with numpy broadcast; result shape = broadcast(lhs, rhs).
ops.docs: tensor.elementwise(%lhs, %rhs) {fn} -> %result. A binary elementwise op over broadcast-compatible tensors (sec-51 elementwise + broadcast). Pure. find_tensor_misuse: operands + result Tensor-kinded (OperandNotTensor / ResultNotTensor); lhs.element == rhs.element == result.element (TensorElementMismatch); `fn` in {add,sub,mul,div,max,min,pow} (FnInvalid); result.shape == shapes_broadcast_result(lhs.shape, rhs.shape) when Compatible (BroadcastResultMismatch), Incompatible -> ShapeBroadcastIncompatible pointing the 3z right-aligned position, Unknown -> ACCEPT (a shape.assert discharges). STRUCTURAL (2 operands, 1 result, `fn` present+String): the generated verify_elementwise.

operands.name: lhs
operands.doc: the left tensor operand (a 3d Tensor: element + shape).

operands.name: rhs
operands.doc: the right tensor operand; its element MUST equal lhs's; its shape broadcasts with lhs's.

results.name: result
results.doc: element == the inputs' element; shape == the numpy-broadcast of lhs.shape and rhs.shape (find_tensor_misuse checks exactness via shapes_broadcast_result).

attributes.name: fn
attributes.doc: the binary op, a CLOSED vocab: add | sub | mul | div | max | min | pow. find_tensor_misuse rejects any other token (FnInvalid).

ops.name: fft
ops.summary: A complex-to-complex FFT along `axis` (direction forward/inverse); complex = SPLIT re/im (two real tensors in -> two out).
ops.docs: tensor.fft(%re_in, %im_in) {direction, axis} -> (%re_out, %im_out). A complex-to-complex FFT along one axis (sec-59 fft leg); complex is SPLIT re/im (two real tensors in, two out) MIRRORING the CKIR c2c split-buffer ABI (NO complex element TypeKind -- a true complex kind is a Dxxx name-forward). Pure (forward+inverse share the graph; the 1/N scale is the caller's, kept out for bit-exactness). find_tensor_misuse: all four operands+results Tensor-kinded (OperandNotTensor / ResultNotTensor); re_in.element == im_in.element == re_out.element == im_out.element (TensorElementMismatch); re_in.shape == im_in.shape (FftInputShapeMismatch); re_out.shape == im_out.shape == re_in.shape -- a c2c FFT preserves shape (FftResultShapeMismatch); `axis` present+Int+>=0 and < input rank (AxisInvalid); `direction` in {forward,inverse} (FftDirectionInvalid). ⛔ element FLOAT + F32-only restriction rides the 22b native provider (name-forward; declare stays element-agnostic like 21b). ⛔ DETERMINISM: an FFT is a reduction TREE -- ORDER-SENSITIVE; the bit-exact contract is CEIR-22's ORACLE GATE (ledger L9). STRUCTURAL (2 operands, 2 results, `direction` present+String, `axis` present+Int): the generated verify_fft.

operands.name: re_in
operands.doc: the REAL part of the complex input (a 3d Tensor; a float element at the provider tier).

operands.name: im_in
operands.doc: the IMAGINARY part; its element AND shape MUST equal re_in's (the split-complex convention).

results.name: re_out
results.doc: the REAL part of the transformed output; a c2c FFT PRESERVES shape+element, so == re_in's.

results.name: im_out
results.doc: the IMAGINARY part of the output; == re_in's element + shape.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.doc: the transform direction, a CLOSED vocab: forward | inverse. find_tensor_misuse rejects any other token (FftDirectionInvalid).

attributes.name: axis
attributes.doc: the transformed axis (>=0, < input rank). find_tensor_misuse: present+Int+>=0 and < rank (AxisInvalid, reused from reduce).

ops.name: matmul
ops.summary: Matrix-multiply the two innermost axes: lhs [..,M,K] x rhs [..,K,N] -> [..,M,N] (the contraction dim must match).
ops.docs: tensor.matmul(%lhs, %rhs) -> %result. Matrix-multiply the innermost axes (sec-51 matmul/batched matmul). Pure. find_tensor_misuse: operands + result Tensor-kinded; lhs.element == rhs.element == result.element (TensorElementMismatch); both ranks >= 2 (MatmulRankInvalid); lhs's last axis == rhs's second-to-last axis (ContractionMismatch, the NEW contraction-dim check class); result.shape == [batch.., M, N] (MatmulResultMismatch). ⛔ DETERMINISM: contractions are ORDER-SENSITIVE (float accumulation order — a tiled/device GEMM ≠ a naive one bit-for-bit); the sec-27/sec-28 determinism CLASS rides the EXECUTING tier — the bit-exact contract is CEIR-22's ORACLE GATE (named-forward, ledger L9). STRUCTURAL (2 operands, 1 result, no attrs): the generated verify_matmul.

operands.name: lhs
operands.doc: the left matrix operand [.., M, K] (a 3d Tensor, rank >= 2); its element == rhs's.

operands.name: rhs
operands.doc: the right matrix operand [.., K, N] (rank >= 2); its second-to-last axis K == lhs's last axis.

results.name: result
results.doc: element == the inputs'; shape == [.., M, N] (the batch dims + M from lhs + N from rhs).

ops.name: reduce
ops.summary: Reduce a tensor along `axis` with `fn` (sum/prod/max/min/mean); result shape = input shape minus the axis.
ops.docs: tensor.reduce(%input) {axis, fn} -> %result. Reduce a tensor along one axis (sec-51 reductions). Pure. find_tensor_misuse: operand + result Tensor-kinded; input.element == result.element (TensorElementMismatch); `axis` present+Int+>=0 and < input rank (AxisInvalid); `fn` in {sum,prod,max,min,mean} (FnInvalid); result.shape == input.shape with `axis` removed (ReduceResultMismatch). ⛔ DETERMINISM: reductions are ORDER-SENSITIVE (float sum/mean/prod depend on accumulation order); the sec-27/sec-28 determinism CLASS rides the EXECUTING tier (a device reduction ≠ a serial one bit-for-bit) — the bit-exact contract is CEIR-22's ORACLE GATE (named-forward, ledger L9). STRUCTURAL (1 operand, 1 result, `axis` present+Int, `fn` present+String): the generated verify_reduce.

results.name: result
results.doc: element == input's; shape == input.shape with `axis` removed (rank one less).

attributes.name: axis
attributes.doc: the reduced axis (>=0, < input rank). find_tensor_misuse: present+Int+>=0 and < rank (AxisInvalid).

attributes.name: fn
attributes.doc: the reduction, a CLOSED vocab: sum | prod | max | min | mean. find_tensor_misuse rejects any other token (FnInvalid).

ops.name: reshape
ops.summary: Reinterpret a tensor under a new shape with the same total element count (shapes_reshape).
ops.docs: tensor.reshape(%input) -> %result. Reinterpret a tensor's elements under a new shape (sec-51 reshape); the target rides the result type. Pure. find_tensor_misuse: operand + result Tensor-kinded; input.element == result.element (TensorElementMismatch); shapes_reshape(input.shape, result.shape) != Incompatible (ShapeReshapeIncompatible), Unknown (dynamic/symbolic total) -> ACCEPT. STRUCTURAL (1 operand, 1 result, no attrs): the generated verify_reshape.

results.name: result
results.doc: element == input's; shape == the TARGET (same total element count as input.shape).

ops.name: transpose
ops.summary: Permute a tensor's axes by `perm` (a true permutation of [0,rank)); result shape = input shape permuted.
ops.docs: tensor.transpose(%input) {perm} -> %result. Permute a tensor's axes (sec-51 transpose). Pure. find_tensor_misuse: operand + result Tensor-kinded; input.element == result.element (TensorElementMismatch); `perm` parses to a TRUE permutation of [0, input rank) (PermInvalid, the declared-words scar); result.shape == input.shape permuted by `perm` (TransposeResultMismatch). STRUCTURAL (1 operand, 1 result, `perm` present+String): the generated verify_transpose.

operands.name: input
operands.doc: the tensor whose axes are permuted (a 3d Tensor).

results.name: result
results.doc: element == input's; shape == input.shape with its member dims reordered by `perm`.

attributes.name: perm
attributes.doc: the axis permutation: comma-separated axis indices (e.g. "0,2,1"), one per axis, a TRUE permutation of [0, rank). find_tensor_misuse: parses to exactly `rank` distinct indices covering [0,rank) (PermInvalid). ⛔ a string (ATTR_KINDS has no int-array), parsed like the work `access` tokens.
